blockers.what: report() can itself throw, and then launch() rejects and node exits 1 ('signals found') without a verdict. String(error) throws for a thrown value with no prototype, and reading error.stack throws for an Error whose stack getter throws. Reproduced with --import load hooks: scan() throwing Object.create(null) exits 1 through the bin and src/index.ts; command.ts module throwing Object.create(null) at load exits 1; an Error with a throwing stack getter prints the okolos-mail: line then exits 1. No code reachable from input throws such a value (no throw, timer or process.exit in scan.ts, render.ts, core-mail, i18n or core-lookalike src), so it is not reachable by a caller today, but it contradicts the launcher's own claim that every failure ends with 2. (apps/mail-cli/src/launch.mjs:175-179 (called from 141 and 148), found by the `unit` tier)

index.ts header says a direct start 'ends the same way' and that every failure ends with 2, but `node src/index.ts` on an engines-allowed node with --no-experimental-strip-types (or NODE_OPTIONS carrying it) exits 1 with node's ERR_UNKNOWN_FILE_EXTENSION before a line runs; on node 20 the same. Unfixable inside the file; dist/index.js and the bin both exit 2 in the same conditions. (apps/mail-cli/src/index.ts:1-11, found by the `unit` tier)

Windows is held by construction only: no test runs on Windows (CI is ubuntu-latest, node 22), and the closed-reader branch keys on code === 'EPIPE'. If a Windows pipe write to a gone reader surfaces as another code (libuv maps ERROR_BROKEN_PIPE to EOF), a scanned verdict ends with 2 and an okolos-mail: line instead of its own code. That direction never yields a false 0 or 1, so it does not violate the node's guarantee. (apps/mail-cli/src/command.ts:122, found by the `unit` tier)
